text: This is Kazuo. It turns the AI subscriptions people already pay for into a network that sells compute by the job, with every job paid in USDC on Arc.
Most of the day, a Claude or Codex subscription sits idle. Kazuo lets its owner run a node, and lets anyone else buy a single job from it.
Every paid job leaves a receipt on chain. This list is read straight from the Kazuo Log contract on Arc.
Here is that contract on the Arc explorer, with registrations, heartbeats and receipts written to it as events.
The job board is where a buyer posts work. It shows recent jobs, and the provider nodes that are live right now.
This node sells Echo and Claude Code at a fixed price per job. It proved its key with World AgentKit, and it is not yet backed by a verified human.
Signing in uses Privy. A person can use an email, or connect an existing wallet. Here we connect a testnet wallet, which signs a sign-in message.
With the wallet connected, World ID Selfie Check can prove a real person stands behind it. World App scans this code to complete the check.
Now we post a job. We pick Claude Code, describe the task, and ask for a quote. The quote names the node, the price, and the address that gets paid.
Paying signs a USDC authorization from the wallet, and a transaction is being signed and settled on chain on Arc. The buyer spends no gas.
The job runs on the provider's machine inside a sandbox, and the answer streams back to this page, with the payment and the result hash beside it.
On the Arc explorer, this is the settlement from this job: one USDC transfer, from the buyer straight to the provider.
And this is the job's receipt on chain, recorded in the Kazuo Log contract with the hash of the answer.
The network page shows how settlement works. The facilitator relays the signed authorization and pays the fee, and receipts are read back from Arc.
On the provider's side, the node shows its earnings and what it sells, and it stays connected to the network waiting for the next job.
That is Kazuo: idle AI capacity, sold one job at a time, settled on Arc, with World and Privy in the loop. Thanks for watching.
